newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January jobless rate at 2.68 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January jobless rate at 2.68 percent.

text.p: Taiwan's unemployment rate stood at 2.68 percent in January, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Monday.
The January rate came in slightly higher than the average forecast of 2.56 percent that resulted from a February 21 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

The polled economists had said they expected January joblessness to remain at comparatively high levels because the relative sluggishness of Taiwan's economic recovery has resulted in a slower rate of job creation.

The January jobless rate came in slightly higher than the average 2.56 percent projection that resulted from a February Reuters poll of Taiwan economists, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said.
The number of unemployed people in January increased 7,000 to 252,000 from December. The number of employed stayed at 9.18 million, some 7,700 more than in January 1996.
Of the unemployed, 58,000 or 6.13 percent came from the agricultural sector, while factory closures forced 16,000, or 0.46 percent, workers to lose their jobs, the agency said.
Employment in the services sector increased 151,000 or 3.21 percent due to a rise in the number of service companies.
Taiwan's jobless rate held close to 1.5 percent in 1991-1994 but rose to 1.79 percent in 1995 and has pushed above 3.0 percent in August, September and October 1996.
The jobless rate averaged 2.60 percent for all of 1996.

Officials have attributed the shift to higher jobless levels to a fundamental change in Taiwan's economy -- a shift toward service-oriented industries from labour-intensive manufacturing that had engendered decades of dramatic economic development.
